pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: A closure uses a variable from its enclosing function. After the closure is created, the enclosing function assigns a new value to that variable. When the closure runs, which value does it see, and why?
expected_points: the new value — closures capture the variable itself, not a snapshot of its value
the closure holds a reference to the shared variable, so reads and writes on either side are visible to the other
the variable outlives the enclosing function if the closure does (it escapes to the heap)

questions.prompt: Sketch the functional options pattern for a constructor and explain what it buys you over a plain config struct parameter.
expected_points: an Option is a func(*T) that edits the value under construction; WithX(v) returns a closure capturing v; the constructor takes ...Option, sets defaults, then applies each in order
a config struct can't distinguish a deliberate zero value from an omitted field, so defaults get ambiguous
new options can be added later without breaking existing call sites, and the struct's fields can stay unexported

questions.prompt: Before Go 1.22, closures created inside a for loop famously all saw the same final value of the loop variable. Why did that happen, and what changed in Go 1.22?
expected_points: pre-1.22 the loop declared one variable for the whole loop, so every closure captured that same variable, which held its final value by the time the closures ran
Go 1.22 gives each iteration a fresh loop variable, so capturing it is safe
the fix or old workaround i := i created a fresh per-iteration copy; the module's go directive decides which semantics apply

questions.prompt: Go has generics, so you can write Map and Filter — yet idiomatic Go still mostly uses plain for loops. When does passing a function as a value earn its place, and when should you just write the loop?
expected_points: function values fit when the function is the varying part of a fixed algorithm: comparators/predicates for stdlib APIs, functional options, deferred cleanup, callbacks
Go has no method-chaining culture and function literals are verbose, so pipelines of Map/Filter read worse and allocate intermediate slices
prefer the plain loop when the body grows complex, needs early exit, or a chain of higher-order calls replaces one clear loop

questions.prompt: In your Counter exercise, inc and reset both work on the same count. What does that make the pair, conceptually — and at what point would you reach for a struct with methods instead?
expected_points: two closures over one variable are shared mutable state — effectively an object whose fields are the captured variables and whose methods are the closures
with several captured variables or several closures, a named struct with methods states the same design more clearly
(bonus) once goroutines exist, shared captured variables become a data-race concern

questions.prompt: WithPort(9090) executes and returns before NewServer ever runs. Explain exactly what WithPort returns and how the 9090 survives until it is used.
expected_points: WithPort returns a closure of type Option (func(*Server)); calling WithPort does not touch any server
the closure captures the port argument, carrying 9090 with it
NewServer later calls the closure with the server under construction, which is when the assignment happens
